The passage describes the division of Korea at the 38th parallel for the purpose of accepting the Japanese surrender after World War II, with the Soviet Union taking control in the north and the United States in the south. This division was intended to be temporary but eventually led to the establishment of separate governments — the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) and the Republic of Korea (South Korea) — and the Korean War solidified this division. Today, Korea remains split near the 38th parallel.
